# bugs #3121: A designator after a positional initializer is misassigned or rejected in an automatic object

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3121/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Confirm the reading of C11 6.7.9p19 under Decision. Then apply the patch and close.
- Patch: [bugs-3121.patch](../../patches/bugs-3121.patch). Applies to r17176 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The declaration in the ticket, `struct S l = { 1, .t = x, .t.l = 41, };` in a function, compiles
with warning 147, and `l.t.l` keeps the 43 of `x.l`. A maintainer says in the ticket that an
earlier patch removed the error 69 of the original report. The code that initializes objects at
run time, as for automatic objects, has more faults with designators:

- After a positional initializer, initializers with designators are assigned to the members in
  order, or the compiler reports error 47, 35, or 69.
- Several initializers for parts of one member, as in `.p.b = 2, .p.c = 3`, each set the rest of
  that member to zero.
- In an automatic array, an element that a designator skips gets no store, and the zero fill can
  overwrite an element that the list initialized.

## Cause

`createIvalStruct` in `src/SDCCast.c` handles designators in a loop that ends at the first
initializer without one, and it initializes the whole member for each of them. It assigns the
rest of the list to the members in order. `createIvalArray` generates the stores in list order and
sets its index from each designator. After the last entry its zero fill continues from the index
of that entry. The data image of static objects is written by `printIval`, which orders the list
with `reorderIlistFull` first.

## Fix

Lists with such designators are ordered with `reorderIlistFull`, which `printIval` uses for static
storage. The new wrapper `reorderIlistCode` in `src/SDCCval.c` also returns, in a separate list,
each initializer for a part of an object that an expression initializes as a whole. In
`src/SDCCast.c` the new `designatedIlist` converts the result into the form that
`createIvalStruct` handles, and `createIvalArray` sets elements without an initializer to zero.
The new `createIvalPart` then stores each entry of the separate list into its part only.

## Decision

The patch and GCC differ for a list that initializes a member as a whole from an expression and
then designates a part of that member, such as `{.t = x, .t.l = 41}` in the ticket's example. The
patch stores 41 into `l.t.l` and leaves `l.t.k` at the 42 that it has from `x.k`. This is how the
patch reads C11 6.7.9p19. GCC sets `l.t.k` to zero. The test checks that member only under
`__SDCC`. The alternative is to follow GCC.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-3121.c` has the ticket's example, designators after positional
initializers, designators with several steps, arrays, a union, and global objects. Each function
with automatic objects runs twice and fills its objects with 0x5a before it returns, so that a
member without a store is not zero by chance. Without the patch the test does not compile for
mcs51 (errors 47, 35, and 69). With the patch it passes on the host, for six mcs51 configurations
(the four models, and small and large with `--stack-auto`), for stm8, and for z80. The regression
suite for mcs51-small has no failures, and the assembly of its other tests is unchanged. valdiag
has no failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, and mcs51-stack-auto.

## Related

- The patch for #2948 changes `designatedIlist` and needs this patch.
- The anonymous union in the ticket's fifth comment is initialized correctly without the patch.
  The test has it as `cb`.
- With the patch, `{.b = 2, .a = 1, 5}` assigns 5 to `c`, the next member without a designator.
  C11 6.7.9p17 assigns it to `b`.
- With the patch, for a union that code initializes, `createIvalStruct` uses the first initializer
  with a designator and ignores the later ones.
